title: Spill-resistant Paged Query Protocol and Index Guardrails
creator: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: dashboard queries are exhibiting expensive cold reads and occasional spill to long-tail storage for large time-range paginated queries. This ticket proposes a spill-resistant paged query protocol that reduces IO amplification by combining lightweight index guardrails, tenant-aware micro-window compaction, and a budget-driven hedging strategy. Goal: decrease 95th/99th percentile latency for multi-page explorations and reduce cascade read amplification during bursty tenant scans without sacrificing freshness or correctness.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile query latency for paginated dashboard views reduced by >= 25% on representative tenant clusters (measured on perf-canary)
Read amplification (IO bytes per logical row) reduced by >= 30% for queries that previously spilled to cold slices
Query responses remain consistent with current API semantics (stable cursor semantics preserved across retries and hedges)
No increase in error rate or out-of-memory events in query workers observed in a two-week canary run
Operational metrics: new telemetry exposes per-tenant spill events, guardrail-trips, hedged-request counts, and tokenized cost budgets
design_decisions: Introduce an 'index guardrail' layer: small bloom/time-hint indices kept hot for recent/active windows that prevent scans from touching deep cold segments when overscan is unnecessary
Micro-window compaction: compact adjacent small time buckets into a read-friendly micro-window for tenants with many small writes; compaction runs are incremental and rate-limited
Budget-driven hedging: queries carry a soft IO budget; when the planner estimates a high risk of spill, system will issue a low-cost hedged probe to an index guardrail before escalating to full scan
Adaptive overscan sizing per-tenant: overscan parameter tuned by recent access patterns and SLA class rather than a global constant
Graceful fallback: if guardrail metadata is stale or missing, fall back to existing pagination path and emit a diagnostic event for automatic repair
Telemetry-first rollout: all feature flags gated and instrumented; rollout by tenant cohort and region with automatic rollback thresholds
implementation_notes: Server-side changes in dashboard-query-service: add index-guardrail cache module with limited memory footprint and LRU eviction
Planner changes: add a lightweight cost estimator that combines index-hit probability (from guardrail) and per-tenant budget to choose between prefetched-window vs full shard scan
Cache invalidation: guardrail entries TTL can be updated by write-paths and compaction jobs; provide an API for asynchronous invalidation after major rollouts
Compaction: implement compaction job in analytics-pipeline with rate limit knobs and non-blocking merge semantics
Telemetry: add metrics and logs (metered in Console) for guardrail hits, false positives, hedged probes, and per-request estimated budget vs actual IO
Testing: unit tests for planner heuristics, integration tests with synthetic tenant workloads, and perf test harness against perf-canary cluster
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Console backend & Analytics teams. Agreed to prototype guardrail cache as in-memory LRU with 256MB budget for canary region.
2026-02-18: Prototype planner implemented; initial synthetic load shows 18% reduction in 95th p99 across small-range paginated queries but no change for large-scan patterns.

2026-02-24: Observed one false-positive pattern where guardrail TTLs were stale after a rapid replay of historical writes. Decided to add an asynchronous invalidation hook in write-path and increase guardrail versioning.
2026-03-02: Integration of micro-window compaction into analytics pipeline MVP. Compaction job running in passive mode (no replacement) to collect compaction benefit metrics.

2026-03-07: Canary rollout to 10 tenants in us-west with feature-flag. Early telemetry: guardrail hit rate 62%, hedged probe rate 8%, estimated IO budget exceeded in 4% of requests triggering fallback; investigating planner tuning.

2026-03-10: Adjusted overscan multiplier for low-SLA tenants; updated acceptance criteria thresholds and scheduled full perf run on 2026-03-16. Next: PR review, more unit tests for eviction edgecases, and on-call runbook draft.
